across the seasonal cycle, setting her eventful existence at various dramatic locations in the grand
theatre of earth, sky, and ocean. Traveller-adventurer, nourisher and protector, artificer and
destroyer, the Cloud clearly models her utterance on that of Hunt’s Nepheliads. But the model
is also a point of departure. S. modifies his principal source to achieve an elemental lyric and
thematic simplicity, varying the stresses and the number of syllables within each of the two basic
line-patterns so as to avoid the monotony that might have resulted from the rhyme-scheme.
